resources.title: Pictures on a timeline
paragraphs_in_document_order: Thursday 21 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Teach a forty-minute picture-ordering lesson for three to four pupils. Two invented object stories each use three generic pictures. Pupils place one set on a simple timeline from first to last, then keep the pictures and one time sentence or selected phrase in a book.

BUILD Weekly - Spring!B42/C42: Order pictures on a simple timeline. Theme: Resilience & Change. Unit, BUILD - Spring!D10: Then & now, how things change. Term assessment, J10: F: ordering tasks.  S: personal timeline produced.

Week 3 is formative. The owner sets Week 6 as assessing. Success is three pictures in the supplied story order, read left to right, plus one accurate time phrase or pointed link. A second set is optional extension.

Set Source Cards pages 1–2, Support Cards page 1, the word mat, visible model and books at each place. Adult may cut six pictures along white gaps and mark the reverse A B C across the top and D E F across the bottom. Keep a full labelled key available. Give three cards from one set at a time. Pupils may point and direct an adult to move cards.

Every task keeps a word bank, sentence starters and visible model. Level 2 describes the requested scaffolds, not a qualification level. Supported, Independent and Aspire retain all supports. Exact scribing and usual aids are available. No public questioning, cold calling or required reading aloud.

Top row: three stages of one bag. Bottom row: three stages of one box. Pictures start in mixed order. The stories are invented for teaching and give the order; they are not histories of actual products. No product dates, makers or places appear. Use shape clues, labels and story words without reliance on colour. A stitched patch, torn ends, wood grain and paint chips give visible cues.
Thursday 21 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A
2 minutes private settle; 8 minutes find and compare whole and torn straps. Keep bank, stem and model visible.
5 minutes sources with a brief reset; 5 minutes bag model and private hinge; 5 minutes guided box timeline.
10 minutes own chosen timeline with a brief reset; 3 minutes private check and response; 2 minutes exit and evidence.

“A timeline shows time order. I start on the left. In this story the strap is whole first. Next it tears. Last it is sewn. I use the story and picture clues.” Move B, C, A onto first, next, last. “You can move the cards, point or tell me where to put them.”

Ask quietly or offer two choices: “Does the sewn strap go before or after the tear in this story?” After. If unsure, reread the last clue and trace torn then sewn. Parallel check: “Does bare wood come before or after paint in the box story?” Before. Keep scaffolds visible and do not use public questions.

Pictures only; no sewing, sharp tools, paint or broken objects are needed. Adult cuts cards if wanted. Touch is optional. Offer HELP/PASS, a quiet request, supported observation or an agreed supervised pause. No pupil needs to disclose personal possessions or experiences.

Pupil chooses a set, directs picture positions and selects a time phrase. Adult moves or writes exactly as directed, reads back quietly and offers keep/change. Record actual prompts and who chose the order. A copied model alone does not establish picture ordering.
Thursday 21 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Supported: choose between two cards for each slot and direct an exact scribe. Independent: order one set and keep one time sentence with all scaffolds. Aspire: order the other set or add a before/after link using the bank, stem and model. Every route finishes a three-picture timeline.

Cognition: one set and one step at a time. Communication: quiet wait time, exact scribe and usual aid; plan in any language. SEMH: predictable steps and private help. Sensory/physical: large cards, adult cutting and optional touch. Shape, position, words and borders carry meaning without colour.

Evidence HUM-BUILD-S1-W03-E1: chosen set, actual picture order, one time phrase or pointed link, clue and help. Use Pupil number: ____ for each pupil; absent pupils stay blank. An actual audience reply, one NS and the pupil’s response in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode precede R. E follows actual banking. Do not pre-fill actual results.

A repair helper keeps a clear record of what happened before and after a repair. Offer authentic words or choices to the Communication portfolio. Do not infer independent reading, writing or award completion from supported sequencing.

resources.title: Staff answers and support
paragraphs_in_document_order: Thursday 21 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A
Order pictures on a simple timeline. From BUILD Weekly - Spring!B42/C42. Thursday 21 January 2027, P3. Theme: Resilience & Change. Formative; Week 6 is assessing under the owner brief.

Top row from left: A sewn strap with patch and stitches; B whole strap; C torn strap with frayed ends. Bottom row: D painted box; E chipped paint; F bare wooden box. Each set has three pictures. The designs and object stories are invented; no product dates or makers are implied.

Starter: B is whole and C is torn. Bag timeline: first B whole, next C torn, last A sewn. Box timeline: first F bare wood, next D paint, last E chips. Use the supplied story clues to justify the order. A point to the torn edge or repair patch with the matching time label is a valid supported response.

Sewn goes after torn in the bag story. Bare wood goes before paint in the box story. If unsure, reread the relevant clue and offer two positions, keeping the model. Recheck privately using the other story.

The printed left-to-right card order is deliberately mixed. Letters identify cards; they are not the time order. A timeline shows when events happen, not object size or colour. A neat-looking repair can come later than damage. Do not generalise that all old objects are broken, or that all boxes follow this story.
Thursday 21 January 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Use the fourth pupil-number field only if a fourth pupil attends. Leave absent pupils blank. Check each pupil places or directs all three cards and selects a time phrase. A shared model alone does not establish individual ordering.

Every task keeps bank, starters and visible model. Adult reads clues quietly if wanted, offers two choices and moves cards only as directed. Scribe exact selected words. Read back for keep/change and record actual prompts. No public questioning or required reading aloud.

Order both sets or add an accurate before/after link. Word bank: before, after, torn, sewn. Starter: __ comes after __. Model: Sewn comes after torn. A second set is extension; one correctly ordered set remains the core finish.

Use HUM-BUILD-S1-W03-E1. Offer authentic responses to the Communication portfolio. Actual audience reply, one NS and the pupil’s own response precede R. Actual banking precedes E. [AWARD] / [QUAL] checks stay separate; no qualification completion is inferred.

Sewn comes before or after torn?
Words: after, torn, sewn.
Start: __ comes after __.
Model: Sewn comes after torn.

shape_text.text: Three pictures tell one made-up story.

slides.notes:
HUM-BUILD-S1-W03 · Year A · Thursday 21 January 2027 · P3
The bag timeline: 5 minutes.
Teacher: Model the bag timeline B C A, reading left to right: first whole, next torn, last sewn. The editable table gives positions and captions. Physically place the three cards on the strip in Support Cards. Quiet hinge: does the sewn strap go before or after the tear in this story? After. If unsure, reread the last story clue and trace torn then sewn. Parallel hinge: does bare wood come before or after paint in the box story? Before.
Outcome verbatim: Order pictures on a simple timeline.

HUM-BUILD-S1-W03 · Year A · Thursday 21 January 2027 · P3
My book timeline: 10 minutes.
Teacher: At minute 25 include a short reset in the ten-minute book block. Each pupil chooses the bag or box story, mixes its three cards and places them left to right on a simple timeline. Supported: offer two choices for each slot and an exact scribe. Independent: order and retain one time sentence using all supports. Aspire: order the other set and add a before/after link with bank, stem and model. Do not remove supports to test independence.
Outcome verbatim: Order pictures on a simple timeline.

HUM-BUILD-S1-W03 · Year A · Thursday 21 January 2027 · P3
Adult support brief: 0 minutes.
Teacher: Hidden adult brief: Level 2 means bank, starter and visible model on every task, not qualification level. Prompt ladder: point, short private prompt, rephrase, choice/scaffold, model first step then return task. Use invented stories and picture clues, not guesses about product age. Touch and cutting optional; adult cuts. Keep three pictures per set. No real dates, makers or personal disclosures. R follows actual reply/NS/response; E follows banking.
Outcome verbatim: Order pictures on a simple timeline.
